s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with recent onset of blurred vision and ocular irritation, following a systemic illness with fever and arthralgia
salient_findings: Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
Localized anterior stromal infiltrate with normal corneal thickness
key_facts: Patient is a teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Recently acquired periorbital hyperpigmentation
Ocular history was negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis had been ruled out
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Aqueous tap PCR results were positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
Aqueous humor was negative for CHIKV-specific immunoglobulins
Positive IgM CHIKV serologic test

shortlist.label: Chikungunya virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive PCR results and positive IgM serologic test

shortlist.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and presence of keratic precipitates

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation

shortlist.label: Adenoviral keratoconjunctivitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular irritation and recent onset of blurred vision

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation, periorbital hyperpigmentation, and recent systemic illness

raw.rationale: The patient's aqueous tap PCR results were positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load and she had a positive IgM CHIKV serologic test, indicating a recent Chikungunya virus infection, which is consistent with her symptoms of bilateral blurred vision, ocular irritation, fever, and arthralgia.

rejected.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not match the typical presentation of Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis, which is a chronic condition with heterochromia of the iris and characteristic iris atrophy.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: The aqueous tap PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses 1 and 2, making Herpes simplex keratitis unlikely.

rejected.label: Adenoviral keratoconjunctivitis
rejected.why: The aqueous tap PCR results were negative for adenovirus, ruling out Adenoviral keratoconjunctivitis.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not match the typical presentation of Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease, which is a systemic condition with granulomatous uveitis, skin, and hair findings, and the patient's primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis had been ruled out.
